agent_notes: The packet's verse 1 includes the superscription (KJV 23:0); the title is translated here together with the first line. Gloss of pos 4 (rō'î): STEPBible gives '[is] shepherd my'; I kept it as 'my shepherd' because the participle with suffix is a noun phrase, 'the one who shepherds me'. The five English versions agree on 'shepherd' except BBE, which paraphrases; I followed the Hebrew.

'lō' eḥsār' is imperfect: 'I will not lack' / 'I do not lack'. KJV's 'shall not want' is correct for its century but 'want' no longer means 'lack'. The literal layer keeps the future-or-habitual ambiguity with 'I will not lack'.

history.note: [consider] Attribute the 'my leader' sense to Meiri (with Ezek 34:31) and present the Egyptian/Mesopotamian royal title as general background, not as something these sources say. (PS.23.1 Meiri: "ה׳ רעי, ע״ד צאן מרעיתי אדם אתם ... ור״ל מנהיגי")

agent_notes: Pos 4 'al: STEPBible 'at'; glossed 'beside' ('upon, by'). Versions split between 'beside' and 'by'; the sense is 'at the edge of'. Rashi (packet) and Meiri/Radak treat ne'ot as 'abode' (nāweh), the shepherd's encampment; 'pastures' is the traditional sense and I kept it in the dramatic layer while the literal layer says 'abodes of grass'.

yešōvēv is Polel of šûv. STEPBible 'he restores'; Rashi reads 'brings back to former state', Radak and Metzudat Zion read 'sets at rest' (cf. Isa 30:15 'in šûvâ and naḥat'). I glossed 'he brings back' and left the layers to carry both senses. nafšî translated 'my soul/self/life'; the literal layer uses 'my soul' since the Hebrew nefesh is the whole living self, and the commentary says so.

Revised after the review: the sentence about the KJV leaving out the resumptive 'they' is gone; the commentary now says the KJV keeps it (as YLT and ASV do) while BBE drops it. 'Shadow of death' versus 'deep darkness' is now presented as two readings, each with its sources, and the advice to the actors no longer contradicts Radak.

Gloss of token 5 (צַלְמָוֶת): STEPBible has 'deep darkness'; I kept it as the gloss but the literal layer says 'shadow-of-death' to keep the compound visible, since the Masoretic vowels and the Targum (טוּלָא דְמוֹתָא) read it so. The choice between the two readings is left open in the commentary.

Tokens 14-15: הֵמָּה is plural and resumptive, 'they, they comfort me'. Radak explains the plural verb with the two named objects (rod and staff). Rashi and Metzudat David read the rod as affliction and the staff as support; Malbim reads both as the shepherd's tools. I presented the pastoral reading as the primary image and mentioned the other as a tradition, without choosing.

agent_notes: dišannātā is a perfect (not KJV's present 'anointest'). Commentators in the packet (Rashi, Metzudat David) take it as a reference to the past anointing as king; Radak and Meiri read it as a figure of prosperity. I rendered it as a perfect and did not choose between these readings. 'dšn' means literally 'make fat', hence 'refresh' in STEPBible; the literal layer keeps 'made fat'. Radak's gloss that Psalm 23:5 'returns from the metaphor' is noted in the commentary only briefly.

history.note: [consider] Present the battle-line overtone as a possible echo of the verb ('arakh milchamah), not as what the verse means. (PS.23.5 Radak: "שיראו בכבודי וירקב עצמם לקנאתם")

agent_notes: wešavtî: the Masoretic pointing is from šûv 'return' ('and I will return to the house of YHWH'), which is what the Hebrew word-for-word gives, whereas KJV, following the Septuagint and Vulgate, read yšb 'dwell' (so 'dwell'). Ibn Ezra, Radak and Meiri (packet) note both: 'repeatedly come back' or 'be at rest' (from šûvâ). I kept 'return' in the literal layer and said 'dwell' in the commentary. Also 'for ever' in KJV for le'orek yamim is 'for length of days', not forever in the strict sense; Radak (packet) takes it as a long life in line with 'all the days of my life'.

history.note: [consider] Mention that the Targum and Radak in the packet also support 'dwell', so the KJV is not alone in reading it that way. (PS.23.6 Targum: "כַּד אֵתֵב בְּבֵית מַקְדְשָׁא דַייָ"; Radak: "או הוא פרושו: ישבתי, כמשמעו")

agent_notes: Нумерация стихов здесь еврейская (PS.23), в Синодальном переводе это Пс 22. В 1-м стихе «Господь» в драматическом слое следует Синодальному переводу, а в буквальном слое оставлено YHWH.

По замечанию рецензента: в комментарии Синодальный перевод процитирован как «направляет меня на стези правды ради имени Своего», оговорка о единственном числе убрана; оставлена мысль, что «стези», как и KJV 'paths', звучит нравственнее, чем «колеи».

В буквальном слое «имени своего» оставлено строчным и без сакральной заглавной: это перевод слов древнееврейского текста, а не принятое в Синодальном написание. В драматическом слое для слуха — «ради Своего имени».

(PS.23.3 KJV: "he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake"; English commentary: "The KJV's 'paths of righteousness'"; Hebrew מַעְגְּלֵי is plural (construct).)

agent_notes: «צלמות» передано в буквальном слое как «тень-смерти / глубокая тьма», в драматическом — «долина смертной тени» по Синодальному переводу; оба прочтения сохранены в комментарии.
В Синодальном переводе «умастил елеем» и «чаша моя преисполнена» — оба выбора близки к еврейскому; «наполнена» в драматическом слое выбрано для естественной интонации.

Синодальный перевод читает «и я пребуду» (по LXX), масоретское «вернусь» — в комментарии и примечании; «хесед» передан как «верность по завету» в буквальном слое и «милость» только в ссылках на Синодальный перевод.
